the plant peroxisomal membrane protein, AtPex1op, is not localized to peroxisome membranes, but instead occurs in subdomain(s) (subcompartment) of the ER.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel plant peroxin that appears to be involved in peroxisomal biogenesis and is localized to subdomain(s) (subcompartments) of ER.
the identification, cloning, and characterization of a plant gene, AtPEX11a, which is required for normal peroxisome biogenesis and development in Arabidopsis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AtPex11p, AtPex12p, and AtPex14p (peroxisome membrane proteins) are involved in peroxisomal membrane biogenesis and that AtPex7p, AtPx10p, and AtPx11p (cytosolic peroxins) are involved in protein body, oleosome, and peroxome biogenesis.

peroxisome biogenesis in plants involves a series of peroxins (AtPex1p, AtPex2p, AtPEx7p, AtPEX10p, and AtPex14p) that are sequentially recruited to ER, possibly in a stepwise fashion, and that peroxisomes are formed from ER-derived vesicles that bud off from the ER.

AtPex1p is an ER-associated protein, not a peroxisomal protein.
